- Document action items and owner for procurement (PO, SOW, legal redlines).
- Schedule a QBR / decision meeting to walk the mutual action plan and answer technical questions.

2) Share mutual action plan + QBR agenda (attached) — Neha to send today.
3) Schedule 60-min QBR with Acme stakeholders — target between 2027-05-18 and 2027-05-20.
4) Procurement/PO submitted — target by 2027-05-28 to enable capacity reservation for June.

Two time slots that work on our side (please let us know your availability):
- Wed 2027-05-19 14:00–15:00 ET
- Thu 2027-05-20 09:00–10:00 ET

I've attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.xlsx) and a short QBR agenda (QBR_Agenda_draft.pdf). Rishi, Marissa — looping you in for pricing and CS context.

Sara, can you confirm: 1) who from Acme needs to be at the QBR (technical, procurement, finance), and 2) whether SOC2 evidence or any procurement paperwork is required ahead of time?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this smoothly.

Best,

Hi all,

Following up with the two commitment options (summary here — full spreadsheet attached):

Option A — Growth Buffer (12-month term)
- +20% committed throughput (guaranteed capacity)
- Modest unit discount (5%) on hosted tokens once committed baseline is exceeded
- No upfront commit fee; month-to-month billing against committed units
- Target customer benefit: minimal upfront spend, preserves flexibility

Option B — Capacity & Term Commit (24-month term)
- +50% committed throughput
- Larger unit discount (15%) and committed-capacity reservation fee credited over 12 months
- SLA: priority capacity scaling and 99.95% regional uptime SLA for committed pools
- Target customer benefit: lower per-unit cost and predictable availability for steady growth

Operational notes:
- Reserved capacity provides guaranteed node allocation; burst-to-shared only when queued capacity is available and according to policy.
- KV/prefix caching reduces effective compute for repeated prompts — we can present expected token-cost delta during the QBR.

I'll attach the detailed pricing matrix (Redwood_Pricing_Commit_Options.xlsx). Neha — recommend we present both options and call out 1) expected monthly spend under current usage, 2) delta under +20% and +50% usage, and 3) onboarding/ops tasks and timing.

-Marshall (pricing) note: if Acme is comfortable with a 24-month commit we can negotiate a faster capacity reservation timeline to secure GPUs for mid-June.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Strategy | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
